hook: Copernicus Sentinel-6B just entered service, continuing a global sea-level record that began back in 1992.

sections.voiceover: Copernicus Sentinel-6B just entered service, continuing a global sea-level record that began back in 1992.
sections.visual_cue: Close-up of a satellite orbiting Earth against deep space.

sections.voiceover: On October 29, 2026, the Copernicus Sentinel-6B satellite entered operational service. Sentinel-6B launched on November 17, 2025, but will it operate through the 2030s?
sections.visual_cue: Graphic showing the launch date and the satellite name.

sections.voiceover: It joins Copernicus Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich, which has been in orbit since November 2020.
sections.visual_cue: Animation showing two satellites trailing each other in orbit.

sections.voiceover: EUMETSAT confirms these twin satellites provide the precise data needed to track global sea levels. These combined missions extend our precise sea-level tracking record well into the 2030s.
The European Commission ensures this vital data collection continues for the next decade.
sections.visual_cue: The Copernicus Sentinel-6B satellite glowing above the blue Earth.
